Executive summaryTromml's Minecart gives R&P a central home for every customer conversation, combining intelligence from field activity, sales and tech support calls, and sales performance across both ERPs. Rather than simply recording that data, Minecart activates it: reps see who to talk to and what to talk about, and the key intel makes it back to management.

This proposal includes initial setup with a 30-day pilot that allows R&P's reps to use Tromml's "system of action" with your own customers and data. Options for this pilot include basic account intelligence, or it can be scaled to include the analysis and incorporation of two years of sales data and call recordings.

Current situation

Running an effective sales team as a multi-line aftermarket supplier requires getting the most out of every rep. But managing and coordinating thousands of unique relationships is challenging, especially when those relationships are happening on calls, at trade shows, and in the field.

Without a system to track these relationships and rep activity, management often struggles to ensure reps are spending their time in the right places and having the right conversations, or that critical signals are surfaced that provide opportunities for better coaching, opportunity detection, and issue resolution for at-risk accounts.

Your ERPs might tell you what is happening, but they give little to no information on why sales have changed and what money is actively sitting on the table.

What this costs

Lack of visibility into sales activity

  • Reps default to checking boxes rather than the conversations that drive sales
  • A slipping or at-risk opportunity goes unnoticed until it's too late
  • Follow-ups and opportunities get missed, and revenue is never captured

Missed signals from market intelligence

  • Escalation of product or service issues gets delayed until revenue is unrecoverable
  • Cross-selling opportunities get missed
  • Trade show opportunities get overlooked
  • Missed customer feedback on campaigns, initiatives, and product releases

The Minecart system

A trommel is the mining machine that separates gold from dirt. At Tromml, we apply the same concept to your data, pulling valuable signal out of customer conversations and sales performance.

We focus on removing time-consuming administrative work for reps and management: digging through dashboards, sorting through meeting notes, and preparing call reports. With our system, conversations are captured through call transcript analysis or simple voice memos, so reps can turn admin time into selling time.

We also make sure what's captured doesn't sit in the system. It gets activated. Notes are processed to pull out follow-ups, identify issues and opportunities at the line level, and make sure key intel is highlighted for the next visit.

Key signals get sent to management in daily and weekly reports. Every note, call, and outcome builds customer intelligence the company owns, keeping customer information up to date and building long-term intelligence that both people and AI systems can act on.

And many more. Minecart finds the answers, so your team can spend the time growing the business.

How it works

The fuel of the Minecart system is our simplified note capture: reps use voice memos (or call recordings) to add key intelligence straight from customer conversations. The note comes back cleaned up, misspellings fixed and details extracted, with no cleanup work and nothing left to log. Tromml's proprietary technology handles the rest automatically: account assignment, follow-up extraction, opportunity detection, and even line-level intelligence across multiple sales units, with key insights surfaced to management.

With sales data integrated, Tromml also helps make sure reps are spending their time on the right accounts, with key sales insights delivered in plain language, not dashboards.

And the intelligence keeps itself current: customer records stay up to date instead of hoping the right field gets updated, and along the way your data becomes AI-ready across every department.

Success criteria

We judge the pilot on five things, and you're the judge:

  • Reps use it: notes and voice memos get captured in the normal flow of the week, without chasing
  • Admin time drops: logging a visit takes seconds, and call reports stop being a separate task
  • The reports earn their read: each manager report surfaces accounts and issues worth acting on
  • Signal turns into action: flagged items become follow-ups, save attempts, and cross-sell conversations during the pilot
  • The analyses tell you something you didn't know: wallet-share movement, recurring issues, and cross-line gaps, in plain language

You keep the pilot insights, regardless of next steps

The sales analysis, the call analysis, and every account history built during the pilot are yours to keep if you decide not to move forward.
